recent.evidence: S4 shows Strait of Hormuz daily transits at 10, 52% below the 30-day average of 21, satisfying the forecast's stated threshold of remaining at least 30% below average during the window.

recent.statement: Natural gas prices (NG=F) will rise by 2.5-3.5% following the EIA weekly storage report release on 2026-07-23
recent.evidence: No signal reports natural gas (NG=F) prices or the EIA storage report reaction at all — only crude oil, equities, and rate-meeting signals — so the specific 2.5–3.5% post-report gain is unsupported after the window closed.

recent.evidence: S4 reports Strait of Hormuz at 10 daily ship transits (52% below its 30-day average) as of 2026-07-23, within the forecast window and below the stated 12/day threshold.

recent.statement: A tropical cyclone will make landfall in Haiti within the next week, causing widespread damage and disruption
recent.evidence: All signals concern cyclones in the Pacific (Dolphin, Genevieve, Fausto) far from Haiti, and none shows any tropical cyclone landfall in Haiti during the window.

recent.statement: The conflict in Ukraine will escalate, leading to a complete shutdown of the Kerch Strait within the next week
recent.evidence: No signal mentions the Kerch Strait or any shutdown there; all signals concern unrelated Southeast Asian chokepoints, and a complete closure of the Kerch Strait would certainly have been captured.

recent.evidence: The current Strait of Hormuz snapshot shows 10 daily transits, 52% below its 30-day average of 21, indicating a sharp decline rather than the forecast 20% increase.

recent.statement: The Strait of Hormuz sees a significant increase in ship transits within the next week
recent.evidence: The latest Strait of Hormuz snapshot shows only 10 daily transits, 52% below its 30-day average of 21, showing a sharp decline rather than a significant increase.

recent.statement: There will be a significant increase in Brent Crude prices by the end of the week.
recent.evidence: The only Brent signal shows 90.12 $/bbl up just 1.22%, a modest daily move that does not establish a significant week-end price increase.

recent.evidence: IMF PortWatch data as of 2026-07-23 shows Strait of Hormuz daily transits at 10, 52% below its 30-day average of 21, exceeding the forecast's 20% reduction threshold.
